Highlands, Camp Holly Fish Camp, Wabasso, West Melbourne,
Melbourne Beach, Grant-Valkaria, Micco, Sebastian Inlet State

...The National Weather Service in Tampa Bay Ruskin has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Florida...

Alafia River At Lithia affecting Hillsborough County.

.Heavy rain of 2 to 5 inches over the past 24 hours will cause the
Alafia River at Lithia to rise above flood stage late tonight.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Alafia River at Lithia .

* WHEN...From late tonight to Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Additional residences downstream of County
Road 640 bridge begin flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:00 PM EST Monday the stage was 9.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 13.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight to a crest of 14.6 feet tomorrow evening.
It will then fall below flood stage Thursday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 14.6
feet on 02/23/1936.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Geneva
Above Lake Harney to rise. The river is forecast to climb through
Minor flood stage and into Moderate flood stage over the next few
days. Rises near Major flood stage will be possible this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Flooding of homes in low lying areas
becomes more significant. Many secondary roads are impassable,
limiting access to homes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 8.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EST Tuesday was 8.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 9.9 feet Saturday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of east central Florida, including the following
counties, Indian River, Saint Lucie, Martin, and Brevard.

* WHEN...From 10 AM EST this morning through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Some
roads may flood. Minor tidal flooding along the coast may be
exacerbated by heavy rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An approaching disturbance from the Gulf is forecast to interact
with unusually rich moisture over portions of Central Florida,
causing bands of heavy rain today through Monday afternoon. The
ground is nearly saturated, especially along the Treasure Coast
urban corridor. Widespread amounts of 1-3 inches are forecast,
with localized amounts of 5 inches or more which may cause flash
flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

International Airport, Royal Palm Estates, Lake Belvedere Estates,

Cypress Lakes and Lakeside Green.

The National Weather Service in Miami has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern Palm Beach County in southeastern Florida...

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 7 feet
in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal portions of Saint Lucie and Martin Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory and High Surf Advisory,
until 7 PM EST Monday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through
late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 1 at 1:39AM EDT until November 2 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 2 at 1:06AM EST until November 3 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents.

* WHERE...San Francisco, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern
Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 PM PST this
evening. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from late tonight
through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.0 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) on
Sunday 11/01 at 3:59 PM. These predictions include up to 1.5
ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Collier County; Inland Collier County; Mainland Monroe
properties.description:
An upper level low will will continue to influence storms in the
Gulf and Bahamas through Monday. With the lack of a strong synoptic
surface forcing mechanism, predictability as to where and when heavy
rain will fall remains low. However, the environment continues to
support the potential for heavy rainfall and slow moving cells.

* WHAT...Heavy rain may cause, or worsen ongoing urban and street
flooding.

* WHERE...All of South Florida

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Isolated to scattered areas of flash flooding will be
possible, with the main impact being street flooding, road
closures, and limited impact to structures in flood prone areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Pockets of very heavy rainfall resulted in localized flash
flooding on Sunday and those areas, and others, have the
potential to be impacted again on Monday. Forecast amounts look
very similar to yesterday, with common amounts of 1 to 3 inches
where showers and storms occur. Scattered locations around south
Florida may see closer to 3 to 5 inches of rain. The more
isolated high end amounts have the potential to peak around 6 to
9 inches. These amounts could accumulate rather quickly, on the
order of 2 to 4 hours.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 7
feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Saint Lucie and Coastal Martin Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 PM EDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 31 at 9:36PM EDT until November 1 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 1 at 2:57PM EST until November 2 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Okeechobee County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 1230 AM EST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 630 PM EST, emergency management reported heavy rain in the
warned area due to thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly. Between 5 and 9 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Treasure Island, Okeechobee, Four Seasons Estates, Taylor Creek,
Whispering Pines, Okeechobee Airport and Basswood Estates.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused the St. Johns River near Cocoa to rise
into Minor Flood Stage. The river is forecast to rise through Minor
flood stage and into Moderate flood stage mid to late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 16.7 feet, Water covers yards, encroaches on homes and
may enter low lying homes along the St Johns River in the Lake
Poinsett area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM EST Monday the stage was 16.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 PM EST Monday was 16.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 16.8 feet Thursday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 29 at 1:51PM EDT until October 30 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Sanford
to rise. The river is forecast to climb into Minor flood stage in the
next couple days, with a continued rise into through late week,
approaching Moderate Flood Stage by the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Water begins to move over sea wall around
Lake Monroe and rises into grassy areas around the sea wall. Water
begins to encroach on Seminole Boulevard.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 5.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tomorrow morning and continue rising to 6.8 feet early Sunday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

mean higher high water. Additional rounds of heavy rainfall will
increase the footprint of saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Until 5 AM EST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Saltwater flooding of low elevation streets and lots
is expected. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less

persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Downstream tidal effects on the St Johns River have slowed flow at
Astor. Heavy rainfall that has occurred  upstream will lead to
additional rises within Moderate flood stage late this week as water
works north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 3.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:30 AM EST Tuesday was 3.4 feet.
- Forecast...While remaining in Moderate Flood Stage, the river is
forecast to gradually decline the next couple days, then rise
again this weekend.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.

Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Brevard County in east central Florida...

* Until 145 PM EST.

* At 1135 AM EST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
15 and 20 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
of 2 to 4 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
already occurring.

Grant-Valkaria. This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK
HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER
GROUND NOW! Life threatening flash flooding of low water
crossings, small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Palm Bay, Melbourne, Malabar, Indialantic, Camp Holly Fish Camp,
West Melbourne, Melbourne Beach, Grant-Valkaria, Micco, Melbourne
Village, June Park, Melbourne Airport, Spessard Holland Park,
Melbourne Shores and Floridana Beach.
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 2 at 11:35AM EST until November 2 at 1:45PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now! This is an extremely dangerous and
life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are
fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

Turn around, don't drown. Be aware of your surroundings and do not
drive on flooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Inland Northern Brevard; Inland Indian River; Inland St. Lucie; Inland Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Inland Southern Brevard; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of east central Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Martin, Coastal Saint Lucie,
Inland Indian River, Inland Martin, Inland Northern Brevard, Inland
Saint Lucie, Inland Southern Brevard, Mainland Northern Brevard,
Mainland Southern Brevard, Northern Brevard Barrier Islands and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An approaching disturbance from the Gulf is forecast to interact
with unusually rich moisture over portions of Central Florida,
causing bands of heavy rain today through Monday afternoon. The
ground is nearly saturated, especially along the Treasure Coast
urban corridor. Widespread amounts of 1-3 inches are forecast,
with localized amounts of 5 inches or more which may cause flash
flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.instruction:

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH MONDAY AFTERNOON

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.eb8f23614741a.title: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 12:39PM EST until November 2 at 3:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Downstream tidal effects on the St John River have slowed flow at
Astor. Heavy rainfall will lead to additional rises within Moderate
flood stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EST Monday the stage was 3.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EST Monday was 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crests of 3.8 feet
just after midnight tonight with additional tidal crest forecast
through Moderate flood stage this week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 10:07AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1130 PM EST.

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.ec317b9486e57.title: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 10:07AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Florida...

Peace River At Arcadia at SR 70 affecting DeSoto County.

.Heavy rain of 5 to 10 inches over the past 24 hours will cause the
Peace River at Arcadia to rise above major flood stage.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Peace River at Arcadia at SR 70.

* WHEN...From this afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Up to 60 homes at River Acres are flooded.
The Woman's Club and American Legion are impacted.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 9.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this afternoon and continue rising to a crest of 17.1 feet
Thursday evening.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.2
feet on 09/11/2004.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
